version.value: Berg’s score for solo violin and orchestra; the edition the performers used is not stated.
version.note: The item description and the 1941 review name the work and the performers but not the printed or manuscript material.

performers.note: Named in the item description and in the 1941 review, which also states that Krasner suggested the concerto to Berg.

date.note: Stated in the description written by the transferring collector, in the Sony Classical box-set listing (Discogs, “Cleveland, Severance Hall, December 15, 1940”) and in the Bach Cantatas Website discography; no session ledger was seen.

place.note: Named in the Sony Classical box-set listing and in the Bach Cantatas Website discography; the Internet Archive description does not name the hall. That discography heads the entry “recorded live”; the issue is the commercial six-side Columbia set, and each file begins and ends in silence, with no applause.

label.value: Columbia Masterworks, set M-465 (written MM 465 in the Internet Archive description)
label.note: The item description reads “Columbia 78rpm Set MM 465”; the 1941 review and the 1942 catalogue give “set M-465”. The review gives three discs at $3.50.

catalogue.value: Columbia Masterworks set M-465; discs 11589-D to 11591-D
catalogue.note: The disc numbers are read from the OCR text of the 1942 catalogue, which lists the set as 6 sides with Krasner, the Cleveland Orchestra and Rodzinski; the page image was not checked.

matrixTakeSides.value: XCO 29764 to XCO 29769 (six sides); the take numbers are not given
matrixTakeSides.note: As given in the item description. Which sides carry the first movement is not stated.

credits.note: Named in the item description, which adds “High bit rate”.

date.value: Not stated; the item was added to the Internet Archive on 17 September 2013
date.note: The public date of the item is an upload date, not the date of the transfer.

processing.value: Digital transfer of the 78 rpm discs, described as high bit rate; equalisation and noise reduction are not described.
processing.note: The item carries one MP3 for each movement, uploaded as the original file.

composition.value: Berg died in 1935, so the work has been in the public domain in the EU and other life-plus-70 countries since 2006; IMSLP also marks it public domain in Canada and in life-plus-50 countries. IMSLP considers it probably still protected in the United States.
composition.note: Rights in the composition are stated separately from rights in the recording.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial EU public domain: first published before 1963; reviewed in September 1941 and listed in Columbia’s catalogue of 1942.
recording.note: The Internet Archive item carries a CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 licence label from the uploader. That label does not meet the site’s licence rules and is not relied on. The United States status of a 1940 recording is not established.

rights.creditLine: Alban Berg, Violin Concerto, I. Louis Krasner, violin; The Cleveland Orchestra; Artur Rodzinski, conductor. Recorded 15 December 1940; Columbia Masterworks set M-465, reviewed in September 1941. Digital transfer by F. Reeder; Internet Archive item BERGViolinConcerto-NEWTRANSFER. Territorial EU basis (first published before 1963); US status not established.
